rationale: Evidence from iteration 8 (score 799.5, best so far): the oval finished 20/20 at 1.88 s, the s-bend finished 20/20 at 2.34 s, and the slalom finished 7/20 (progress 0.82 mean, 13 off-track exits). Lowering mass and body_length in iterations 7 and 8 is what moved the slalom from 0 to 7 finishes, so reduced yaw inertia is the lever that is working. Iteration 8 also made the gentle tracks worse: oval and s-bend steering_oscillation rose to 0.17 and 0.36, control effort rose, oval line-loss events reached 1.0 per trial, and oval and s-bend times got slower. This fits the hypothesis from iteration 8 that the lighter robot is over-responding, so the remaining slalom failures are at least partly overshoot on reversals. Changes: (1) kd 1.0 to 1.1, to add damping against the faster yaw response; (2) mass 0.5 to 0.45 kg, a further step in the same direction as the change that helped the slalom, which cuts yaw inertia by roughly 10 percent. Body length (0.12 m), body width, wheel geometry, sensors, weights, kp 3.0, ki 0.05, base_speed 1.5 and last_direction are unchanged, so the effect of these two changes can be read against iteration 8. I did not narrow wheel_track: that would raise effective steering gain by about 20 percent, which is close to the kp 3.5 change that did not help in iteration 6. Expected result: slalom finishes rise from 7/20 toward 10 or more, with progress above 0.9, and oval and s-bend oscillation stay at or below about 0.2 and 0.35. Hypotheses: (a) if the oval or s-bend lose finishes or oscillation rises above 0.4, the lighter robot is still over-responding and kd should rise to about 1.2 with mass held at 0.45; (b) if slalom progress stays under 0.85 with off-track exits, the next lever is wheel_track narrowed to 0.10 m to add yaw authority, paired with kp back at 2.8 to hold the effective gain; (c) if the slalom finishes at 15 or more of 20 with oval time under 1.9 s, base_speed can be tested at 1.6 for the time term. Measurements wanted: completion, progress, completion_time, rms_error, max_error, line_loss_events, steering_oscillation, control_effort.
